note: OBLIGATIONS WE HAVE DEFERRED, and the condition that makes each one due. 18% of startups fail on legal challenges — almost never because somebody decided to ignore a rule, and almost always because a deferral was never revisited. A decision to wait is legitimate. A decision to wait that nobody re-examines is just forgetting with extra steps.
law: Every deferral carries a TRIGGER — the specific, checkable condition that ends the deferral. A deferral with no trigger is not a decision, it is a hope. Deferring is fine; deferring without a trip-wire is not.

items.obligation: Confirm that depicting Pokémon card imagery, set names and product photography in a commercial product is defensible.
items.why: Universal community practice, card images sourced from the standard community API with attribution. No revenue yet.
items.trigger: ANY of: the first dollar of revenue · a paid tier · sponsorship or ads · a cease-and-desist of any kind · media coverage large enough to be noticed.
items.note: This is the one that ends the company rather than costing it money. Everything else on this list is a bill.

items.obligation: Have the giveaway structure reviewed: no-purchase-necessary, AMOE, official rules, the Canadian skill-testing question, and the 65% cash-out clause.
items.why: Structure was built to sweepstakes shape from the start and documented. Berries are unpurchasable, which keeps it out of lottery territory.
items.trigger: ANY of: the first draw with a non-Tyler participant · any prize over $500 · any entry method that could be read as consideration · operating across a border.
items.note: Running a raffle wrong is a regulatory problem in every jurisdiction at once, and the first live draw is the moment it stops being theoretical.

items.obligation: Resolve whether displaying PokemonPriceTracker-derived prices publicly is permitted on our tier.
items.why: Free tool, no revenue, development phase. Their terms reserve commercial use for the $99 tier and describe lower tiers as personal and development use.
items.trigger: The first dollar. Also: any claim on our surfaces that the data is commercially licensed.
items.note: The realistic downside is being cut off, not sued — which is an operational risk, and worst at launch.

items.obligation: Clear the name before any name-coupled spend.
items.why: Nintendo holds a live registration for GOTTA CATCH 'EM ALL in the software class; eight candidate names researched.
items.trigger: ANY of: spending money on the name (merch, print, paid ads) · incorporating under it · a trademark application · significant public traction under it.
items.note: Cheap to change now, expensive later, and the cost curve is steep rather than gradual.

items.obligation: Decide what we collect, where it lives, and what we say about it — before we collect anything personal.
items.why: We hold nothing personal. Watchlists and modes are localStorage and never leave the browser; the newsletter list is one address, Tyler's own.
items.trigger: ANY of: a login · a stored email beyond the newsletter · anything tied to a Discord identity · analytics that identifies an individual.
items.note: Currently our strongest position — we cannot leak what we do not hold. It stops being true the moment auth ships.
